text: Egg-shaped, cone-like clusters three to five inches long, rusty and downy, that split in September and October to let rose-red seeds hang out on slender threads.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray-brown, soft and furrowed, easily bruised by mowers.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long and three to six wide, oval with a point, the edges smooth and often wavy. Shiny yellow-green above, paler and hairy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-yellow, tulip-like, two to four inches long and only slightly fragrant, at the twig tips from April to June. The leaves often hide them.

label: Fruit
text: Knobbly, cone-shaped, two to three inches long, red when young and brown when ripe, when red-coated seeds hang from it on slender threads.

label: Bark
text: Orange-brown, deeply furrowed into ridges that run straight, curve or fork.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long, glossy dark green, pointed and smooth-edged, on thin stalks one to two inches long that bleed milky sap when snapped.

label: Flowers
text: After the leaves, on separate trees: tiny male flowers in dangling clusters one to two inches long, and round green female heads three-quarters of an inch to an inch across.

label: Fruit
text: A wrinkled, yellow-green ball four to six inches across, like a large grapefruit. Inedible, and it oozes a milky latex when cut.

label: Stems
text: Gray-brown, deeply fissured and peeling in strips on old stems.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, oval with a long tapering tip, dark green above and lighter beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, two-lipped, funnel-shaped flowers held upright in pairs along the stems from late April, turning from white to yellow as they age.

label: Fruit
text: Round, glossy dark red berries a quarter inch across, in pairs along the stems.

label: Bark
text: Scaly, furrowed and reddish brown on old trunks; smoother and gray on the branches.

label: Needles
text: Soft, bright green, about an inch long, in tufts on short spur shoots and singly along the new shoots. They turn yellow-amber in fall and drop.

label: Young cones
text: In spring the young seed cones stand up beside the new needle tufts, a crimson that early gardeners took for blossoms.

label: Cones
text: About an inch and a half long, upright, reddish brown, with scales covered in brown hairs.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown, with flat ridges between shallow reddish-brown furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Six to eighteen inches long, once or partly twice divided into seven to fifteen coarsely and irregularly toothed leaflets.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch, bright yellow, star-shaped flowers with red centers, in loose sprays a foot or more long, in July. Falling, they carpet the ground gold.

label: Lanterns
text: Papery, three-sided pods an inch and a half to two inches long, like little paper lanterns, green turning yellow and then light brown, hanging on into winter.

label: Bark
text: Red-brown, peeling in long, narrow, fibrous strips that often leave ashy gray patches.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny scales a sixteenth of an inch long, in opposite pairs or threes, pressed along the twig in four rows, dark blue-green and shiny. Each has a small gland. Often brownish green in winter.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small yellow to orange-brown pollen cones at the branch tips of male trees in late winter.

label: Cones
text: Round, berry-like, a quarter inch across, blue under a white waxy frost, abundant on female trees. They ripen in their first fall and hang on through winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and olive-brown when young, turning light silvery gray with flat ridges in a diamond pattern.

label: Leaves
text: Twelve to eighteen inches long, with five to eleven broad, mostly smooth-edged leaflets, the one at the tip the largest. Black walnut's leaves have many more, toothed leaflets.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins up to six inches long hang as the leaves open in May and June; the female flowers sit in clusters of three to nine.

label: Nuts
text: Round, in a smooth green husk that turns brown and splits in fall. The nut, up to two inches long, has a thin, wrinkled shell.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray with pale lenticels when young. With age it forms narrow, flat-topped, pale ridges in a diamond pattern, between dark gray to black furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Ten to twenty inches long, with 11 to 19 leaflets including one at the tip, crowded toward the ends of the branches so they seem whorled.

label: Catkins
text: Slender yellow-green male catkins two and a half to five and a half inches long; the female flowers are short spikes at the branch tips.

label: Nuts
text: Oblong and pointed, an inch and a half to over two inches long, in a green husk with two to four ridges and short sticky hairs, ripening in September and October.

label: Stems
text: Gray to blackish, smooth, with knobby lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long, oval with a point, toothed but not spiny, hairy along the veins beneath. They drop in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers tucked in the leaf axils in late spring, on separate male and female plants.

label: Berries
text: Quarter-inch, bright red berries crowded along the stems of female plants from late summer, lasting on the bare branches into winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray to almost white, often warty or splotched with red and tan lichens.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, thick and leathery, evergreen, with spiny teeth along the edge and a spine at the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers from April to June, on separate trees: the males in clusters of three to twelve, the females alone or in twos and threes.

label: Berries
text: Bright red, sometimes orange, on female trees from September, lasting into February.

label: Stems
text: Smooth and gray, many stems together.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, up to an inch and a half long, flat and glossy dark green, smooth-edged except for a few small teeth near the tip. No spines.

label: Flowers
text: Small and easily missed, in May and June, on separate male and female plants: the males in little clusters, the females in clusters or alone.

label: Berries
text: Pea-sized, jet-black and glossy, on female plants, ripening in September and lasting into November.

label: Stems
text: Smooth, gray to gray-brown.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, broad and rounded with a short point, lopsided at the base and toothed on the upper half, with five to eight pairs of veins. Pale and downy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Four long, narrow, twisted petals like ribbons, yellow to red depending on the variety, on the bare branches from late January into March.

label: Seed capsules
text: Fuzzy capsules that split open in four, browning as they ripen.

label: Bark
text: Gray to gray-brown, with furrows between short, irregular ridges, often scaly.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, of five to eleven leaflets, usually seven to nine, two to five inches long, toothed and short-stalked, with a few hairs beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small clusters of tiny flowers in spring, dark purple, on the bare twigs before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Clusters of winged samaras an inch to an inch and a half long and a quarter to half an inch wide.

label: Bark
text: Light gray to yellow-brown and corky, deeply furrowed between short, pointed ridges that join in a tight net of diamonds.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, in opposite pairs, usually of seven leaflets three to five inches long, smooth-edged or nearly so, dark green above and whitish beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Tight clusters of tiny purplish flowers without petals, on separate male and female trees, on the bare twigs in April and May before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Drooping clusters six to eight inches long of flat, single-winged samaras up to two inches, shaped like canoe paddles. They ripen in fall and may hang on all winter.

label: Winged twigs
text: Green twigs lined with flat, corky wings. The bark of large old stems is gray or brownish gray and slightly furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, oval, finely toothed, in pairs or nearly so. Medium to dark green, turning brilliant red in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small, four-petaled, yellow-green flowers in threes in the leaf axils, easily overlooked.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch red capsules that split in fall to show seeds wrapped in a fleshy orange-red coat, eaten by birds.

label: Bark
text: Thick, dark gray, broken by furrows into small square blocks like a checkerboard. One of the easiest trees to name in winter.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, broadly oval and pointed, smooth-edged, glossy above and paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small, fragrant, white to greenish-yellow bells in late spring, usually on separate trees: male flowers in twos and threes, female ones alone.

label: Fruit
text: Round, an inch to an inch and a half, yellowish to pale orange with a waxy bloom, the green sepals still at the base. On female trees from September to December.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown, peeling in long, showy strips.

label: Needles
text: Three-quarters of an inch long, awl-shaped and four-angled, curving in with a slight twist, spiraling around the shoot. They stay four or five years and may bronze in winter.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small, oblong, scaly pollen cones in clusters near the branch tips.

label: Cones
text: Small, round and brown, like little rosettes bristling with points, at the tips of the shoots, alone or in groups.

label: Leaves
text: Up to three and a half inches long, glossy dark green, shallowly lobed on the upper half and toothed.

label: Flowers
text: Small five-petaled white flowers in clusters about two inches across, smelling unpleasant to us and attractive to the midges that pollinate them.

label: Fruit
text: Small red haws that ripen in September and usually hang on well into winter.

label: Leaves
text: Glossy dark green, wedge-shaped and widest toward the tip, where they are toothed. Orange to scarlet to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch white flowers in flat clusters two to three inches across in April and May. Pleasant at first, the scent soon turns fishy, which draws the midges that pollinate them.

label: Haws and thorns
text: Small, deep red haws, each holding one to five hard stones. The long, straight thorns are seldom far away.

label: Stems
text: Smooth brown bark with pale lenticels, on stems that zigzag from bud to bud.

label: Leaves
text: Rounded, with a heart-shaped base and doubly toothed edge, softly hairy on both sides.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-brown male catkins hang on the bare stems all winter and turn yellow as they shed pollen at its end. The female flowers show only a tuft of red styles.

label: Nuts
text: Round nuts about an inch across, one to five together, each in a short, leafy husk, released when they ripen in late summer.

label: Stems
text: Smooth and bright red, most striking in winter when the leaves are off.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval to lance-shaped, smooth-edged, in opposite pairs, the veins curving toward the tip as in all dogwoods. Orange to red to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small dull white flowers in flat-topped clusters in early summer.

label: Fruit
text: White berries with a blue tinge, quickly taken by birds.

label: Stems
text: Gray to grayish brown on older stems, dotted with many small lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Two to three and a half inches long, narrow, in opposite pairs, dark green above and pale to nearly white beneath, the veins curving toward the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Quarter-inch, four-petaled creamy flowers, stamens as long as the petals, in rounded clusters at the ends of the branches.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch white berries, each with one or two stones, on stalks that turn red in fall and early winter.

label: Bark
text: Gray to brown, peeling with age in small, irregular plates that leave patches of tan and orange.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, smooth-edged, in opposite pairs, dull green above and lighter beneath, often with tufts of reddish-brown hairs where the veins meet.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters of short-stalked yellow flowers, each cluster with four drooping bracts, on the bare stems in late winter and early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Red to purplish-red, oval, about a quarter inch long, in fall. Edible but very astringent.

label: Stems
text: Gray and somewhat peeling, developing furrows with age.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches long, oval and pointed, smooth-edged, glossy bright green, in pairs or threes around the stem.

label: Flowers
text: Round heads an inch and a half across, packed with tiny fragrant creamy tubes whose long styles stick out like pins in a cushion, from June to August.

label: Seed balls
text: The heads harden into reddish-brown balls of tiny nutlets in August and September, usually hanging on through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray between raised, corky warts.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, narrow and pointed, mostly without teeth, lopsided at the base. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish flowers in April and May with the new leaves, the male ones in clusters and the female ones single.

label: Fruit
text: Small drupes on long stalks, orange-red ripening deep purple from August to October, sweet and thin-fleshed around one round seed.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown and scaly, in thin plates rather than the ridges of northern catalpa.

label: Leaves
text: About ten inches long and six wide, heart-shaped and slightly downy, in pairs or threes. Crushed, they smell unpleasant; northern catalpa's do not.

label: Flowers
text: Frilled white bells in sprays six to twelve inches long, marked inside with two rows of yellow spots and many purple ones; a little later and more purple-spotted than northern catalpa's.

label: Pods
text: Long, narrow pods up to fifteen inches, dark brown in fall, splitting lengthwise to release seeds from October.

label: Bark
text: Tight and gray, in smooth, rounded, interlacing ridges with shallow furrows, on young and old trees alike.

label: Leaves
text: Nine to twenty inches long, dark yellow-green, with five to seven toothed leaflets three to six inches long.

label: Catkins
text: Greenish-yellow male catkins up to six inches long hang with the new leaves; the female flowers are short spikes with feathery reddish stigmas.

label: Nuts
text: Husks an inch and a half to three inches across, green turning yellow and then brown, splitting into four in October around one thick-shelled nut.

label: Bark
text: Scaly on young trees. With age it separates into narrow, flat plates one to three feet long that curve away from the trunk at both ends.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to fourteen inches long, usually of five broad, pointed, finely toothed leaflets three to seven inches long, the one at the tip the largest.

label: Catkins
text: Greenish-yellow male catkins three to five inches long hang in May; the female flowers are short spikes.

label: Nuts
text: A round husk an inch and a half to two inches across, green turning deep brown, that splits in four to free a light tan, flattened nut with sweet meat.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, in narrow, scaly ridges broken into rectangles.

label: Leaves
text: With 9 to 17 lance-shaped, toothed leaflets, often curved like a sickle. Black walnut has more and shorter leaflets.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male catkins about four inches long in April and May; the female flowers are shorter spikes.

label: Nuts
text: Oval pecans one to three inches long, tan to brown with dark streaks, in a husk that dries from green to brown and splits into four in fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth with shallow cracks on young trees; with age, flat, sharp-edged ridges that cross in diamonds and X's.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, usually of five toothed, lance-shaped leaflets three to six inches long, the ones at the tip largest. Smooth or nearly so beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male catkins two to four inches long in April and May; the female flowers are very small.

label: Nuts
text: A thin, often pear-shaped husk about an inch long, green turning brown, that splits in fall to release a tan, slightly flattened nut.

label: Bark
text: Granite gray, faintly tinged yellow, smoother than most hickories'. Smooth at first, it breaks with age into a flat network of narrow, plate-like scales.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long, with five to nine long, narrow, toothed leaflets, dark yellow-green above and lighter beneath, a little downy on the veins.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins three to four inches long hang from last year's shoots or the base of the new growth in spring; the female flowers are short spikes at the shoot tips.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Nuts
text: Round, about an inch, in a thin husk with four winged seams from the tip to about the middle. The kernel is very bitter. Trees seldom bear before thirty.
